Market stance

The group heads into midterm week cautious — DiCarlo flags the first red monthly close for SPY and QQQ, iain calls the weekly charts a disaster, and Prof sees a Sunday-night pump running straight into resistance — while Enrich's watchlist and DiCarlo's semis breakdown keep the focus on which names hold support and reclaim their averages after Friday's rout.

Key watches

Catalysts

  • U.S. midterm elections, Tue 11/3 — the week's centerpiece for every trader in this window; Prof's Iran-post thread and his “most awaited week of 2026” post both point at it
  • Earnings Mon 11/2: AAPL + PLTR — Enrich's list and iain's watch both open with these two (TEM and AEHR also on Enrich's Monday list)
  • Earnings Tue 11/3: AMD — the make-or-break print for Remz's $500 line (SMCI, ANET, SHOP, PFE and ALAB also on Enrich's Tuesday list)
  • JOLTS + factory orders, Tue 10 AM ET — Enrich's macro line for Tuesday, alongside the midterms
  • Sunday-night pump into resistance — Prof, Nov 2, 01:42 UTC: the overnight bounce Enrich warns is “exactly how you get traders leaning the wrong way” — “Let the opening move prove itself”
  • IREN earnings (date not stated) — Prof: earnings must push IREN above $28 “or else its done for sometime”

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
A midterm-week window with the group leaning cautious after Friday's rout. DiCarlo supplies the cycle read: SPY and QQQ monthly closes just printed red — “the first sign of a cycle coming to an end. But I’m not worried. Yet.” iain supplies the chart read: some weekly charts are “an absolute disaster” in transition, mean-reversion bounces are only “short pops into declining MAs,” and his own plan is tiny size, tight risk, buying against pivots with quick trims — “trade like a mosquito dodging flyswatters.” Prof supplies the tape read: a Sunday-night pump “right into resistance” during midterm week, while Enrich warns the same bounce is a trap — “Trap bulls → trap bears → repeat. Friday’s price action sucked in shorts. If this overnight gap-up holds, they’re trapped next.” His longer read is patient: a market selling off because companies are investing in their next decade of growth “could be handing patient investors one of their best buying opportunities in years.” Venu supplies the discipline read for corrections: watch stocks holding above their 50-day average with relative strength and tight action, and remember O’Neil's rule that 3 out of 4 stocks follow the market — so market direction decides most trades. Remz, meanwhile, opened his first November trade in $SPX on Robinhood's 24/7 trading — no level stated. Your process gives no clean qualifier today: the watchlist names fell 5–11% on Friday, SPOT's new 3-month high is strength but not a confirmed breakout (the 52-week high sits 10.66% above), and AMD's $500 line is a test to survive, not a setup to chase. The discipline is in the framing: hold-support and reclaim-EMA tests (MU on its 30-week line, PLTR on its 50-day line, AMD on $500) decide the week, while INTC, IREN, RKLB and NBIS are called out as broken or at their lows, not entries.

From the group

Sean — no new post in this window: his newest visible post is still the Oct 29 system post (“Over the last two days you've learned my entire system…”, quoted to the visible cutoff) and “Unprofitable traders look for a reason to take a trade every day. Profitable traders look for a reason to sit on their hands until their A+ setup is right in front of them.” No ticker, no level — so Sean has no row today, and readability is not the constraint, content is.

iain — sizing and pullback rules, no new ticker: Nov 2, 00:26 UTC — “option 1: sit on my bum and mind my business. or option 2: trade like a mosquito dodging flyswatters. ...tiny size, stupidly tight risk, buy against pivots, quick trims into strength. currently, not trying to swing for the fences when the market can barely throw me a strike.” Nov 1, 21:00 UTC — his pullback-buying checklist: strong stocks in the strongest sectors and themes, clear relative strength vs the indexes and peers, favorable conditions with improving breadth, and a constructive weekly chart (quoted to the visible cutoff).

Enrich — market comments beyond the watchlist: Nov 2, 01:35 UTC — “Trap bulls → trap bears → repeat. Friday’s price action sucked in shorts. If this overnight gap-up holds, they’re trapped next.” Nov 2, 03:25 UTC — “A market selling off because companies are investing in their next decade of growth could be handing patient investors one of their best buying opportunities in years.” His massive-week earnings list beyond the rows: Monday TEM and AEHR, Tuesday SMCI, ANET, SHOP, PFE and ALAB, plus JOLTS and factory orders Tuesday at 10 AM ET — the Wednesday-onward portion is truncated in the visible post and is not guessed here.

Remz — Discord and an SPX trade, no new ticker call: Nov 2, 01:39 UTC — “Being able to trade $SPX on Robinhood 24/7 is a game changer. Just opened my first trade of November.” No level stated. His Nov 1–2 posts are otherwise Discord discount notices (a code at 8 PM EST, code “TTP” for 30% off).

Venu — correction discipline, no new ticker: Nov 2, 02:55 UTC — how to identify the next leaders during corrections: stocks holding above their 50-day average while the market struggles, relative strength, tight price action, lighter selling volume, and accumulation on higher volume (quoted to the visible cutoff). Nov 1, 20:09 UTC — O’Neil on corrections: 3 out of 4 stocks follow the market, so market direction is the first filter (quoted to the visible cutoff).

Prof — politics posts, no trade call: Nov 1, 19:19 UTC — a report that Netanyahu is pressing Trump to strike Iran immediately after Tuesday's midterms, per Axios (his report, not verified here); Nov 1, 21:30 UTC — a Zelensky/Netanyahu comparison post; Nov 1, 23:27 UTC — “Welcome to the most awaited week of 2026.” None of these carries a ticker or a level, so none becomes a row.

Logged-out X shows only the ~5 most recent posts per account, and several posts are truncated in the extraction itself (iain's earnings list and pain-trade post, Enrich's watchlist tail and massive-week list after Wednesday, Remz's DELL tail, Venu's O’Neil post) — they are quoted only to the visible cutoff, never completed by guesswork. Prof's Oct 31 Iran post and his flush-then-rally post were covered yesterday and are not repeated as rows; the flush thesis is carried into the SPY panel only as labeled prior-window context.
  • Price data: Yahoo Finance daily data, as of the Fri Oct 30, 2026 close — this run is Monday pre-market, so Friday's close is still the latest completed equity close. Every distance-to-trigger in this feed uses the regular close. Trader-stated = a level or call from their post, attributed by name. Chart check = computed by us from that data — it can confirm or push back on a trader's framing, and it's labeled every time. Remz's INTC “30%” figure and Prof's Iran report are quoted as theirs, unverified here. No after-hours price is stated anywhere in this window, so no after-hours line appears in any panel. BTC trades weekends, but its as-of here is the Fri Oct 30 close for consistency with the equity names.
  • Sector lines: each card's sector/industry ETF comparison (Yahoo Finance, Fri Oct 30, 2026 close) — close, day change, Weinstein stage by the same 30-week MA method, and price vs the 50-week EMA. Mappings: AAPL→XLK, MSFT/PLTR→IGV, NVDA/MU/INTC/ON/AMD→SMH, GOOGL/META/SPOT→XLC, AMZN/TSLA→XLY, RKLB→UFO, NBIS→CLOU, SKHY→XLI (Industrials — best-fit standard sector ETF for an aviation-infrastructure name), BE→ICLN, DELL→XLK, IREN→WGMI (Bitcoin miners — best-fit industry ETF for a bitcoin-mining name), BTC→IBIT. Best-fit choices are noted here, not hidden. SKHY's own 30-week read is unavailable (Yahoo series starts Jul 10, 2026, 17 weekly closes) — its sector line still carries XLI's own stage.
  • Where none of the seven commented on an index, the section says Unavailable / no trader signal — never “unchanged.” IWM and TLT are unavailable this window: no trader mentioned small caps, bonds or rates. SPY and QQQ carry DiCarlo's monthly-red read plus iain's and Prof's cautious market posts.
  • Qualifier rules (constructive pullback into a key MA/support, tightening base near highs, confirmed breakout; never extended/chased). No name fires as a clean qualifier today: the watchlist names fell 5–11% on Friday, SPOT's new 3-month high (+6.50% on 1.84x volume) is the strongest print but is not a confirmed breakout while the 52-week high 656.68 sits 10.66% above, and AMD's $500 line, MU's 30-week line and PLTR's 50-day line are tests to survive earnings and the open, not entries to chase. Broken or at their lows, not entries: INTC (−28.58% Friday on 4.62x volume), IREN (new 52-week low, below Prof's $28), RKLB (63.57% under its high), NBIS (on its 3-month low). Constructive holds, not entries: AAPL (at the highs), MSFT, TSLA (above every average).
  • Coverage note: nothing is carried over silently. Yesterday's pharma qualifiers LLY, PFE, GILD and MRNA drop because today's posts do not repeat those calls — PFE appears only inside Enrich's Tuesday earnings list, which is calendar, not a call. Yesterday's VRT, RKLB, BE, NBIS, ON, NOW and SPCX rows from Oct 31 are likewise not repeated except where today's posts re-list the name (RKLB, NBIS, BE, ON are re-listed today and get fresh panels). DiCarlo's SPY $760 level from Oct 30 is not carried over — it is superseded by his new monthly-red read. Prof's flush-then-rally post is the one prior-window item carried, labeled as such in the SPY panel, because it still frames the week.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended/avoid). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. INTC and IREN show no invalidation row: with Friday's close the new 3-month / 52-week low, there is no long thesis below to invalidate.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition. No trader posted a retrievable chart image for a covered name in the visible posts this window, so no trader chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line's endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all 70 computable lines passed within 0.5% (SKHY's 30-week MA and 50-week EMA have no history and are not plotted). The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only.
